previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for shortness of breath and a recent fall. Evaluation revealed hyponatremia likely due to poor oral intake and solute depletion, which improved with continued peritoneal dialysis and fluid management. A urine culture showed >100,000 CFU/mL of gram-negative rods, and she was treated with a 7-day course of Bactrim for a complicated UTI. A nuclear stress test ruled out cardiac ischemia as the cause of dyspnea. Constipation was managed with enemas and initiation of polyethylene glycol. She remained stable, sodium normalized to 130, and she was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor electrolytes, and follow up with her primary team. Orthostatic hypotension was noted and attributed to diabetic neuropathy, with counseling on slow position changes.
